messages:
marco: hi team — need a quick one. Hospital discharged my wife with an order for skilled home therapy starting today (PT x3 visits). Home agency says they cant start without an auth and the e-card we have only shows member ID (no group #). Theyre refusing to accept screenshot. Any quick options so therapy isn't delayed?

sara (People Ops): sorry to hear — we can help. Short: for same-day starts ask the agency to request an expedited review (72-hr) and to accept a temporary coverage letter + e-card screenshot. We can also call the insurer provider line to confirm eligibility and get a verbal authorization reference.

marco: can People Ops issue a letter right now? hospital billing is pushing back.

sara (People Ops): yes — we can generate a rapid coverage verification letter (PDF) with member name, DOB, member ID, note that group number is available and being updated, and state the service (skilled home therapy PT) is approved pending prior auth. Bring the letter plus the signed physician order and the agency should accept that for immediate start. I can do this in ~30 minutes.

eric: vendor tip — agencies sometimes accept a phone-verification if you call the insurer with member ID and get a rep name + reference. If provider notes that on intake they usually start treatment and follow with a written auth. Take screenshots of the call confirmation.

benefits-bot: automated note — expedited prior auth turnaround: 24-72 hours typically. For urgent medically necessary home health (post-acute), ask agency to submit "expedited review" and include signed physician order, plan of care, and expected visits. Keep any phone reference numbers.

marco: perfect. can you paste a short coverage letter template i can show to intake?

sara (People Ops): paste this copy/paste: 

```
[Redwood Inference 3 People Ops]
Date: [MM/DD/YYYY]

To whom it may concern,

This confirms that [Member Full Name] (DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY], Member ID: [########]) is enrolled in Redwood Inference's group health plan (Plan: Redwood Choice PPO). A prior authorization request for skilled home therapy (physical therapy) has been submitted and is pending; insurer provider services has been contacted for expedited review. Please accept this letter, the signed physician order, and a screenshot of the digital insurance e-card as temporary proof of coverage to allow the above-named member to begin therapy on [service date].

If additional verification is required, please contact the insurer provider line at [Insurer Phone] and reference member ID [########]. For People Ops assistance, email people-ops@redwood.com.

Sincerely,
People Ops
```

marco: awesome — i'll print and bring it. one more Q: if agency starts and auth later denies, are we on the hook?

sara (People Ops): if denied later, keep the signed order, agency notes, and any phone confirmations. Forward the EOB/denial to people-ops@redwood.com and well help with appeals or getting a retro auth. In emergency/discharge-to-home cases carriers often process retroactively when documentation is supplied.

eric: PSA — get agency NPI and billing name before they start. If they bill under a different DBA the claim can bounce; having that info upfront avoids rebilling.

marco: DMing you agency name + NPI now. thank you all!! :pray:

sara (People Ops): Received — calling insurer now and will upload the letter to you when done. Keep any intake screenshots and the signed order.

benefits-bot: reminder — save phone rep name and reference, screenshot auth letters, and keep timelines: appeals windows vary by carrier (30-180 days).
